title: HessianAdaptiveStochasticConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a globally convex, differentiable function over a convex body C in Euclidean space, with a minimizer xstar in C. The gradient is differentiable and the Hessian is ρ-Lipschitz on C; strong convexity is not required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A gradient query returns g(x,ω), with E[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x) and E[‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²]≤σg² on C. Each call uses a fresh IID seed.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: A Hessian query returns a full symmetric PSD operator H(x,ω), with E[‖H(x,ω)−∇²f(x)‖op²]≤σh² on C. Hessian unbiasedness is not required. Each call selects either a gradient or a Hessian; no function values are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Gradient variance is bounded by σg²; Hessian mean-square operator-norm error is bounded by σh². Only second moments are required, with σg,σh≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: Hessian estimates may be biased, while every returned Hessian must be symmetric PSD. Gradient estimates must be unbiased.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is ℝ^d with Euclidean norm; Hessian errors use the induced operator norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information comprises d, C, x0, D, ρ, and σg. The Hessian error bound σh and accuracy ε are hidden from algorithm construction, although they determine the execution budget. D,ρ,ε>0, x0∈C, and diam(C)≤D. Hessian Lipschitz continuity is required only on C.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianAdaptiveStochasticConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must satisfy E[f(output)−f(xstar)]≤ε, with an integrable objective gap and measurable output.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output belongs to C for every random realization.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective guarantee averages over algorithm randomness and IID oracle randomness under a fixed total oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The convex constrained objective is standard, but the combination of potentially biased PSD Hessian estimates, an unknown Hessian error bound, and separate stochastic derivative queries defines a specialized oracle formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Convex Minimization with Hessians

We consider minimizing a convex function f:Rd→R over a nonempty compact convex set C, where d is a nonnegative integer. The gradient is differentiable everywhere, and the Hessian is Lipschitz on C. At each query, the oracle returns either an unbiased stochastic gradient or a possibly biased, symmetric positive semidefinite Hessian estimate, using independent, identically distributed samples. Both estimates have bounded mean-square error on C. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ lying in C for every realization and satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where x⋆ minimizes f on C and expectation includes oracle and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). We use the Euclidean inner product and norm on Rd; ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The parameters satisfy D>0,ρ>0,σg≥0,σh≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives only d, C, a given point x0, D, ρ, and σg; σh and ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set and minimizer). The set C⊆Rd is nonempty, compact, and convex, and x0∈C,∥x−y∥≤Dfor all x,y∈C. There is a fixed x⋆∈C such that f(x⋆)≤f(x) for every x∈C.

Assumption 2 (Convexity and Hessian regularity). The function f is differentiable on Rd, its gradient is differentiable on Rd, and f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)(x,y∈Rd, t∈[0,1]). Its Hessian satisfies ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤ρ∥x−y∥,x,y∈C.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient and Hessian estimates). Let ν be a probability measure on a measurable sample space Ω. The maps g:Rd×Ω→Rd,H:Rd×Ω→L(Rd,Rd) are jointly measurable, where L(Rd,Rd) is the space of linear operators equipped with its operator norm and Borel sigma-algebra. For every x∈C, g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, and both squared error norms below are integrable. They satisfy Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σg2,Eξ∼ν[∥H(x,ξ)−∇2f(x)∥op2]≤σh2. For every x∈C, ω∈Ω, and u,v∈Rd, ⟨u,H(x,ω)v⟩=⟨H(x,ω)u,v⟩,⟨u,H(x,ω)u⟩≥0.

At call k≥0, the algorithm chooses a point x∈Rd and requests either g(x,ξk) or H(x,ξk). The samples (ξk)k≥0 are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law ν; the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence. Each request returns only the selected estimate and counts as one call toward a common budget. Queries may be made throughout Rd, while the stated oracle error and positivity conditions apply on C.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and belong to C for every realization. The objective gap must be integrable and satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle sample sequence.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f:Rd→R has differentiable gradient and ρ-Lipschitz Hessian on a compact convex body C of diameter at most D; x0,x⋆∈C, x⋆∈arg⁡minCf, D,ρ,ε>0. Jointly measurable oracles use IID samples of law μ under P, with ∫g(x,ω)dμ=∇f(x), ∫∥g(x,ω)−∇f(x)∥2dμ≤σg2, and ∫∥H(x,ω)−∇2f(x)∥op2dμ≤σh2 on C. Hessian samples are symmetric PSD pointwise and may be biased; the stated moments are integrable. Target: measurable feasible output w with integrable gap and ∫[f(w)−f(x⋆)]dP≤ε.

Stochastic convex optimization with adaptive Hessian-noise tuning: HessianAdaptiveStochasticConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) HessianAdaptiveCubic (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(Q[1+log⁡((1+σh/(ρD))Q)]2) gradient and Hessian calls in total; two gradients and one Hessian per round.
(2) (Agafonov, Ashabokov, Kamzolov, et al. 2026), Thm. 5.1, Alg. 2 (M=ρ) O(1+σg2D2ε2+σhD2ε+(ρD3ε)2/7) total gradient and Hessian calls; same three calls per round. (1): Updates need no σh; stopping budget still does. Matches polynomial orders, with squared-logarithmic overhead. (1): Extra logarithm squared and larger leading constant; independent gradient/Hessian samples instead of allowing shared samples.
(3) Extra-Newton (Antonakopoulos et al. 2022), Thm. 3.2 (γ=D); unbiased-Hessian subclass O(1+σg2D2ε2+(σhD2ε)2/3+(ρD3+β0Dε)1/3) total gradient and Hessian calls. (1): On the unbiased PSD overlap, Hessian term (σhD2/ε)1/2 instead of (σhD2/ε)2/3; curvature (ρD3/ε)2/7 instead of (ρD3/ε)1/3, up to log squared. Gains matter when these dominate gradient noise, allowing for logarithms. Scope: biased PSD Hessians. (1): Needs ρ,σg in updates; requires PSD samples. (3) needs neither noise levels nor ρ.
(4) (Agafonov, Ashabokov, D’yakonov, et al. 2026), Thm. 4.1 and App. F.4; unconstrained, exact-gradient special case O(1+log+⁡max{η0,τ¯0}ρR+δ+log+⁡τ¯0η0+(ρR3ε)2/7+δR2ε) total calls, including gradient trials. Global ρ-Lipschitz Hessian; uniform error ∥H−∇2f∥op≤δ. (1): Supports constraints, stochastic gradients and RMS Hessian error. Full classes are incomparable; no established rate improvement. (1): Requires known ρ,σg and bounded C. (4) already adapts to ρ,δ and additionally covers generalized Hessian smoothness.

Abbr: σg,σh≥0: gradient and Hessian RMS errors; PSD: positive semidefinite. Q=1+σg2D2/ε2+(σhD2/ε)1/2+(ρD3/ε)2/7. One call returns one gradient or one Hessian. β0>0: Extra-Newton scale initialization. R=∥x0−x⋆∥ (at most D on the overlap); δ: uniform Hessian error; η0>0: initial regularization; τ¯0=max{4δ,2ρ∥∇f(x0)∥}; log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t}.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Body
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.ContinuousLinearMap

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.HessianAdaptiveStochasticConvex

abbrev Point (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

structure Public where
  d : ℕ
  C : ConvexBody (Point d)
  x0 : Point d
  D : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  σg : ℝ

structure Params extends Public where
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  σh : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : Point p.d → ℝ
  xstar : Point p.d

def IsPSD {d : ℕ} (H : Point d →L[ℝ] Point d) : Prop :=
  (∀ x y, ⟪x, H y⟫ = ⟪H x, y⟫) ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ ⟪x, H x⟫

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Bool × Point p.d
  Reply p := Point p.d × (Point p.d →L[ℝ] Point p.d)
  Output p := Point p.d
  publicInput p := p.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.ρ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σg ∧ 0 ≤ p.σh ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    p.x0 ∈ p.C ∧ ∀ x ∈ p.C, ∀ y ∈ p.C, ‖x - y‖ ≤ p.D
  admissible p I O :=
    I.xstar ∈ p.C ∧ IsMinOn I.f p.C I.xstar ∧ ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ I.f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (gradient I.f x) x) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient I.f) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, ∀ y ∈ p.C,
      ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient I.f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient I.f) y‖ ≤ p.ρ * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    ∃ (g : Point p.d → p.Ω → Point p.d)
      (H : Point p.d → p.Ω → Point p.d →L[ℝ] Point p.d)
      (p0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k) (p0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, hessian, x) ω =>
            if hessian then (0, H x ω) else (g x ω, 0) } ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧ Measurable (Function.uncurry H) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, Integrable (g x) (p0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(p0 : Measure _) = gradient I.f x) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2) (p0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient I.f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(p0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σg ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C, ∀ ω, IsPSD (H x ω)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C,
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖H x ω - fderiv ℝ (gradient I.f) x‖ ^ 2) (p0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.C,
      ∫ ω, ‖H x ω - fderiv ℝ (gradient I.f) x‖ ^ 2 ∂(p0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σh ^ 2)
  successful p I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ (∀ ω, output ω ∈ p.C) ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => I.f (output ω) - I.f I.xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, I.f (output ω) - I.f I.xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HessianAdaptiveStochasticConvex
